sources.title: DocVQA (Mathew et al.)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: 50K questions on 12K+ document images with 9 reasoning-type categories; 80-10-10 split; ANLS metric (+accuracy); baselines (LoRRA/M4C/BERT-QA) vs human 94.36%: structure-sensitive questions are the gap; dataset+code+leaderboard open; WACV 2021.

Reporting discipline: ANLS, never bare accuracy alone (OCR-substring upper bounds inflate). Because DocVQA uses public-source documents and extractive answers, evaluation of later pretrained foundation models should separately audit possible pretraining overlap and shortcut behavior; the DocVQA paper itself does not measure contamination prevalence or assign a risk level.
claims.context: Edition-level analytical synthesis by the Work operator (lineage/selection/boundary/contract judgment, not a literal statement of the cited source); structural home for edition rationale.

claims.text: ANLS (Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity, adopted from ST-VQA) is the primary metric so minor OCR-error mismatches are not severely penalized; used alongside Accuracy.
claims.context: DocVQA paper §5.1 Evaluation Metrics. No threshold/case-folding claim (ST-VQA-side detail, not DocVQA).

limitations.text: Extractive-shortcut vulnerability is a source-supported design concern; possible web-document pretraining overlap is an edition-level audit concern, not a paper-measured contamination rate.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.
